Hello Mervin and Lesley, 
I spoke with Steve from Expedited Service (Steve is the head of our service division in NY), and Steve reviewed the 
service order and spoke with Chris. It was apparent from the service that there was no issue with the Precor hardware. 
further, Chris was able to review Mike's installation and noted that there were no mistakes made by Mike. 
Chris utilized an RF meter and found that there was a low signal from the input. The Precor AMT 885 P80 console has a 
suggested minimum of 60 B.F.'s (it is a high-definition tuner by default), and the signal was below that. Chris attempted 
to run the unit redirect to Set Box, but there were no alternate Set Boxes to connect to in an effort to circumvent the 
low signal. I was also informed that Chris checked the wire, too. 
As per Chris, he did spend time on the phone with Precor Tech Support: during this call it was established that a 
different configuration be utilized to attempt to get the console to receive a signal. I am guessing this is where Metwin 
stepped in and programmed the configuration with Precor Tech Support. 
Chris did take a service log from the machine via USB, which reads all error codes. So if anything else should arise or 
seem like it needs attention, we can review that initial data. 
I apologize as I know the process was inconvenient, but I hope that this clarifies the circumstances and reflects that 
the Precor product itself is not compromised.

will do our best to avoid conflicts with the vacation and holiday schedule of New 
Canaan Public Schools. 
•

Sundays and we will schedule away from conflicts with the YMCA 4th grade 
league. We will look to play two games in consecutive time slots when available 
to minimize travel time.

Dear Parents: 
Fall Sports are in full swing but we need to also focus on the next sports season which is 
basketball. We are excited to announce that there will be new opportunities for players 
looking to play more advanced basketball in addition to playing in our normal YMCA 
recreation league. 
The details are as follows: 
• 
We are currently planning two teams of approximately 10 players. This may 
change subject to participation. 
• 
Teams will be entered in the winter league of the Brewster Sports Center 
(www.brewstersportscenter.com ) about 30 minutes from New Canaan. They 
offer a competitive league in a well-run sports facility. 
• 
The season will begin in mid-to- late November and last until late March. We 
will do our best to avoid conflicts with the vacation and holiday schedule of New 
Canaan Public Schools. 
• 
Games and most practices will be played at various times on Saturdays and 
Sundays and we will schedule away from conflicts with the YMCA 4th grade 
league. We will look to play two games in consecutive time slots when available 
to minimize travel time. 
• 
Participation in the YMCA league will be a requirement to play this additional 
basketball. 
• 
The season will consist of 12 regular season games (plus playoffs) at Brewster 
plus additional games in and around New Canaan with local Fairfield and 
Westchester teams. Total sessions are expected to be about 16-20 games plus 
practices (10+). 
• 
Teams will be coached by experienced, high level coaches with a focus on 
EFTA_R1_00695597 
EFTA02094696

fundamentals and player development. 
• 
Approximate cost will be $400 and will include: uniforms, coaches, practice 
facilities, league fees, referees, insurance and all necessary equipment and 
supplies. 
Tryouts will be on Saturday October 18 from 12 to 3 pm at the New Canaan YMCA. 
They will be conducted by an experienced, independent third party to ensure fairness. 
You must register for Y-Ball in advance in order to participate in the tryouts.
